subject: Age estimation using hierarchical ordinal logistic model

messages.author: d4ef91a20a9b73e6
messages.subject: Age estimation using hierarchical ordinal logistic model
parts:
Hi everyone,

Being a inexperimented modeller, I would like to ask a review of my analysis.

I am trying to estimate the age of some animals based on their teeth status. I thought to use the ordinal logistic model described in Jackman 2009, p: 410.
https://books.google.ch/books?id=QFqyrNL8yEkC&printsec=frontcover&dq=Bayesian+analysis+for+the+social+sciences&hl=fr&sa=X&ei=eBH4VPj1DIThONySgdgB&ved=0CB0Q6AEwAA#v=onepage&q=Bayesian%20analysis%20for%20the%20social%20sciences&f=false

In the populations we study, we can know the age of the animals only when they are juvenile or immature. Otherwise, we report the teeth abrasion status (7 levels). Thus we can work with 9 different age levels. With recapture, we can use the time since the first capture as the explanatory variable of the teeth abrasion. Like the interview example of Jackman 2009, I consider the age at the first capture like the interviewer heterogeneity. Indeed, the teeth of an old individual will be considered differently compared to the ones of a young one.

However, I am more interested in modelling the age before the first capture than correcting the individual heterogeneity. In that sense, I prefer to correct the independent variable, by adding an estimated correction (age before first manip) than the response variable. I am not sure if this is correct, because this variable is not random, as expected for such heterogeneity. We have more and more individuals with known age (close to 0) and this variable cannot be negative.

I have added the script and the txt file. Some improvements still to be done on the initialisation as the model need to be relaunch some times... The chains converged rapidly and the estimations are making sense. Could you please tell me if the mathematical background is ok.

#function to create data at initialisation for age before ringing
datasim <- function(data2){
    dataAge2sim <- array(NA,length(data2))
    for(i in 1:length(data2)){
        dataAge2sim[i] <- ifelse(is.na(data2[i]), runif(1,0,15),NA)}
return(dataAge2sim)}

sink("ms3.jags")
cat("
model {

    for(i in 1:N){  ## loop over observations
          ## form the linear predictor
          mu[i] <-(x[i]+before[id[i]])*lin

          ## cumulative logistic probabilities
          logit(Q[i,1]) <- tau[1]-mu[i]
          p[i,1] <- Q[i,1]
          for(j in 2:8){
                logit(Q[i,j]) <- tau[j]-mu[i]
                p[i,j] <- Q[i,j] - Q[i,j-1]   
          }
          p[i,9] <- 1 - Q[i,8]
          y[i] ~ dcat(p[i,1:9])  ## p[i,] sums to 1 for each i
    }
    ## priors over lin parameter
    lin~ dnorm(0,0.0001)

    ## hierarchical model over known age 
    for(k in 1:NID){
          before[k] ~ dnorm(0,eta.tau)}

    eta.tau <- 1/pow(sd,2) 
    sd ~ dunif(0,3)

    ## priors over thresholds constraint to be ordered
        for(i in 1:7){
    tau0[i]~dunif(tau[1],15)}
    tau[2:8] <- sort(tau0)
    tau[1] <- tauJ*lin}

     ",fill = TRUE)
sink()
# Bundle data
jags.data <- list(NID=NID,x=data$age_after_firstmanip,y= data$age_Teeth,id=id,N=N,tauJ=tauJ,before= age_before_firstmanip)

# Initial values 
inits <- function(){list(before=datasim(age_before_firstmanip),tau0 = runif(7,1,15),lin=rnorm(1),sd=runif(1,0,3)) }  

# Parameters monitored
parameters <- c("before","lin", "sd","tau")

# MCMC settings
ni <- 5000
nt <- 3
nb <- 2000
nc <- 3

# Call JAGS from R 
ms3 <- jags(jags.data, inits, parameters, "ms3.jags", n.chains = nc, n.thin = nt, n.iter = ni,  n.burnin = nb, working.directory = getwd())

TauJ is the known age for the first threshold.

Thank you
